title: Comparing Differential and Multidimensional-Linear Data Complexity
summary: The available truncated-differential formula does not settle the extreme regime, leaving a fair data-complexity comparison between classical differential and multidimensional-linear attacks unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine and fairly compare the data complexities of a chosen-plaintext classical differential attack and its known-plaintext multidimensional-linear counterpart when $s=q=n-1$. In this regime, the classical differential distinguisher is memoryless, whereas the multidimensional-linear distinguisher requires huge memory; when the latter's data complexity approaches the full codebook, its time complexity is also too high. The available truncated-differential data-complexity formula does not determine this comparison, so an alternative analysis is required.

scope.domain: Block-cipher cryptanalysis comparing classical differential and multidimensional-linear attack complexities.
assumptions: The parameter regime is s = q = n - 1.
parameters: s, q, and n — parameters defining the analyzed regime, constrained by s = q = n - 1
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine a fair data-complexity comparison between the two attacks in this regime through an alternative analysis.

citations.label: Links between Truncated Differential and Multidimensional Linear Properties of Block Ciphers and Underlying Attack Complexities

progress.summary: The source contrasts a memoryless classical differential distinguisher with a huge-memory multidimensional-linear one, whose time cost is also too high near full-codebook data. It calls for further investigation because formula (5) cannot provide the data-complexity comparison.
